name: Project Jupiter (Stargate Santa Teresa campus)
owner: BorderPlex Digital Assets and STACK Infrastructure (Blue Owl)

investment_usd.unit: USD (industrial revenue bond amount approved; EDD slide: $21B real estate + $144B furniture, fixtures and equipment)

power_mw.unit: MW (design capacity, Bloom Energy gas fuel cells)

power_source.value: Private microgrid, not connected to El Paso Electric. First planned as 700-900 MW of gas turbines rising to 1 GW; in 2026 switched to Bloom Energy natural gas fuel cells (air permit pending at NMED, decision deadline Nov 23, 2026). Energy Transfer gas pipeline delayed to Feb 1, 2027.

water_use.value: Developer estimate at approval: ~10 million gallons to fill the four buildings over two years, then ~7.2 million gallons/year (avg 20,000 gal/day, max 60,000). Water rights later bought from a sod farm west of Sunland Park.

tax_break.value: Doña Ana County industrial revenue bonds (~$165B) with 95% property tax abatement for 30 years, plus LEDA gross receipts tax share. EDD: current property tax on the land ~$55,427/yr.

community_deal.value: PILOT ~$12M/yr ($360M over 30 years) to the county; first $50M of GRT proceeds dedicated to water/wastewater in southern Doña Ana County ($10M for partners); $6.9M community investments per El Paso Matters.

opposition.what: Empowerment Congress of Doña Ana County and two residents sued the county in 3rd Judicial District Court (filed Oct 17, 2025), saying the $165B IRB approval rested on an incomplete application in violation of county code
Commissioner of Public Lands Stephanie Garcia Richard denied permission for the natural gas pipeline across state land
Commissioner Susanna Chaparro voted against the IRBs (4-1) after three failed motions to delay; residents shouted 'recall' after the vote

New Energy Economy (air permit hearing) and Center for Biological Diversity (emergency water well authorization) petitioned the NM Supreme Court; the court paused both in late August 2026, then unanimously denied both petitions and lifted the stays on Sept 17, 2026
More than 30 protests filed with the State Engineer against the Santa Teresa water well authorization; hearings likely next year

scrutiny.what: NM Department of Justice investigating fake public comments supporting the air permit, filed with residents' names without permission

news.title: $165 billion Project Jupiter data center near El Paso to move forward
Oracle sends force majeure notice on its New Mexico Stargate data center
Project Jupiter: where the AI data center project stands in NM

notes: One record for the whole four-building campus. Oracle says the campus remains on schedule for 2028 despite its force majeure notice. Confirmed: NM Supreme Court lifted its August stays on Sept 17, 2026 (ABQ Journal); NMED must appoint a new air permit hearing officer after Max Shepherd recused. Water pumping for construction resumed. Status of the 3rd Judicial District IRB lawsuit not checked in pass 2. Oct 15, 2026: Oracle and Yucca Growth Infrastructure said a design refinement filed with NMED cuts permitted emissions about 35% (GHG from ~8.8M to ~5.7M tons/yr) with a cap on fuel-cell output; IT capacity unchanged; air permit still under NMED technical review (release reprinted at https://www.grantcountybeat.com/nm-news/non-local-news-releases/project-jupiter-microgrid-cuts-permitted-emissions-by-35-including-greenhouse-gases-in-response-to-nmed-review-and-public-comment).
pin_address: YGI Microgrid (Project Jupiter) air permit 10883 site coordinates, 3.6 mi S of Santa Teresa (NMED legal notice)

name: Meta Los Lunas Data Center

jobs_promised_build.unit: skilled trade workers at peak construction

power_source.value: PNM grid with Meta-paid renewables. 25-00048-UT adds Star Light (100 MW solar + 100 MW battery, Valencia Co.), Four Mile Mesa (100 MW solar + 100 MW battery, San Juan Co.) and Windy Lane (90 MW solar + 68 MW battery, De Baca Co.). community_deal.value: Meta pays full cost of water and wastewater service; $6.2M+ to Valencia County-area schools and nonprofits

Socorro County approves one-year moratorium on data centers amid Green Data Center opposition

news.title: Grant County residents raise alarm over secretive proposed data center
One Southern New Mexico county eyes big incentives for data center as another mulls a block
A new data center proposed in Grant County and more

notes: Public legal notice in Silver City Daily Press Aug 27, 2026. On Hurt Cattle Co. ranch land near Hachita and Playas. At an October county meeting the developer described it as a solar project with possible future gas plant and data center, under 25 acre-feet/yr water. Searchlight first-article date approximate (mid-September 2026). Air permit not yet filed as of late Sept. Pass 2: owner Site Layer 1 LLC has a New York City address; manager AirLayer Advisory LLC (Delaware). Site about 4.5 miles NE of Playas along NM 9. Notice estimated nearly 1.3 million tons/yr of greenhouse gases. Air permit filing was slated for Oct 1, 2026 (ABQ Journal); whether it was filed not confirmed. KRWG (Oct 14, 2026): Granite Renewables says it is 'still feasibility phase' and holds an option on the land; much of the land planned for solar.

name: Roswell Information Park (proposed off-grid data center)

power_source.value: Off-grid, on-site natural gas; Desert Mountain Energy gets a 5% fee on all gas the facility uses

acres.unit: acres leased (about; 14 acres reserved for a possible DME battery plant)

news.title: Desert Mountain Energy signs long-term lease agreement with Roswell Information Park developer

notes: Promoted from lead nm-chaves-desert-mountain-roswell-info-park. Landowner/lessor Desert Mountain Energy Corp. (TSX.V: DME); 25-year lease plus 5-year option. Release quotes the Roswell-Chaves County EDC calling it a 'hyperscale AI data center'; NM EDD and the EDC sent letters of support. No MW, investment or construction date disclosed. A tracker names developer Sustany LLC (not confirmed). Separate from Zenith Volts (20 miles south of Roswell). Size not confirmed against the 20 MW bar; kept as a site on the 'hyperscale AI' description.

notes: 505 Marquette Ave NW, downtown Albuquerque; 225,000 sq ft of colocation space across two facilities (https://h5datacenters.com/albuquerque-data-center.html). Size test: no MW published, so it counts as a large colocation campus on floor area (100,000+ sq ft rule, pass 3).
